events.caption: Sister kinetochores attach to opposite spindle poles and the duplicated chromosome aligns at the metaphase plate.
Sister chromatid cohesion is released and the existing chromatids, now daughter chromosomes, move to opposite poles.

scientific_simplifications: One already-duplicated chromosome, not an entire genome or ploidy count.
Centromere/kinetochore and spindle are schematic; molecular cohesion cleavage not shown.
Same two physical chromatid objects persist, then are called daughter chromosomes after separation.
No DNA replication or homolog pairing occurs in this clip.
